blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit b…

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

blocks.text:
The coverage run (sh-46) is still going. Meanwhile, let me continue the review:

1. Check `Skill` class — `skill.manifest.operative`, `skill.filePath`, `skill.name` fields exist.
2. Check the `read` tool name and 'path' argument in the actual tool registry.
3. Check `effectiveContextWindow` exists in agent_loop scope.
4. Look at pinned_operative_test.dart (compaction) and open_requests_test.dart (+1).
5. Check the read tool call path — ToolCall.arguments typing.

Also verify the E6 behavior claim: "carriers render only when a compaction/trim boundary exists" — and the interplay with `findCutPoint` keeping ~200 recent tokens: the summary user message sits at the position of the fold; carrier right after it. But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

Also — SkillManifest parsing: `frontmatter['operative']` — what parses the frontmatter into a Map? If the YAML parser resolves `operative:` list items — items are strings. `'$item'` conversion handles non-strings (numbers). OK.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

Wait — actually, let me double check: maybe agent_cli.dart or somewhere sets `operativePinNotice = ...`. My grep covered lib/ bin/ flutter_app/lib/ for operativePinNotice outside operative_pins.dart and found only agent_loop.dart references (the import + use). So no host sets it. Confirmed.

- AC6 notices: `SkillOperativePins.diff` never called in production → supersede/drop notices never rendered anywhere. AC6's "reports the change" unmet. IMPORTANT.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

Let me also check `Skill` class shape and the `read` tool. And `effectiveContextWindow` function.

with open('coverage/lcov.info','w') as out:

print('files:',len(files))
EOF

# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \

blocks.text:
The coverage run (sh-46) is still going. Meanwhile, let me continue the review:

1. Check `Skill` class — `skill.manifest.operative`, `skill.filePath`, `skill.name` fields exist.
2. Check the `read` tool name and 'path' argument in the actual tool registry.
3. Check `effectiveContextWindow` exists in agent_loop scope.
4. Look at pinned_operative_test.dart (compaction) and open_requests_test.dart (+1).
5. Check the read tool call path — ToolCall.arguments typing.

Also verify the E6 behavior claim: "carriers render only when a compaction/trim boundary exists" — and the interplay with `findCutPoint` keeping ~200 recent tokens: the summary user message sits at the position of the fold; carrier right after it. But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

Also — SkillManifest parsing: `frontmatter['operative']` — what parses the frontmatter into a Map? If the YAML parser resolves `operative:` list items — items are strings. `'$item'` conversion handles non-strings (numbers). OK.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

Wait — actually, let me double check: maybe agent_cli.dart or somewhere sets `operativePinNotice = ...`. My grep covered lib/ bin/ flutter_app/lib/ for operativePinNotice outside operative_pins.dart and found only agent_loop.dart references (the import + use). So no host sets it. Confirmed.

- AC6 notices: `SkillOperativePins.diff` never called in production → supersede/drop notices never rendered anywhere. AC6's "reports the change" unmet. IMPORTANT.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

Let me also check `Skill` class shape and the `read` tool. And `effectiveContextWindow` function.

blocks.text:
Now I have a good picture of the production code. Let me review the test files and then think about correctness issues.

Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **`injectOperativePinCarriers` anchoring bug**: The carrier is inserted after the LAST renumbering boundary. But wait — the boundary search finds the LAST boundary in the window, then the carrier is placed right after it. But if the boundary message is a `ToolResultMessage` and the next message is also a `ToolResultMessage`, anchor extends. Hmm, the loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
This extends anchor while both current and next are tool results. OK.

But here's a deeper issue: the injected carrier is a `UserMessage` with content = block. If the NEXT message after anchor is a `ToolResultMessage` (e.g., boundary is a user message but following messages are tool results — wait, tool results follow assistant tool calls, and boundary ToolResultMessage extends anchor to the end of the result run, so next after anchor can't be a tool result... actually if boundary is a UserMessage and next message is a ToolResultMessage — can that happen? UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage without an assistant message in between? In a well-formed conversation, tool results come right after the assistant's tool-call message. A UserMessage wouldn't be directly followed by a ToolResultMessage. After tool-pairing repair, orphan results get repaired. Hmm — the repair runs AFTER the injection ("Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window had an orphan tool result at the head... Actually injectOperativePinCarriers runs before repair; boundary = a lone ToolResultMessage (structured hidden marker) — anchor stays at boundary if next message is not ToolResultMessage. Then carrier UserMessage inserted between boundary tool result and whatever follows. If what follows is... the boundary ToolResultMessage's pairing is already satisfied (the tool_use stays visible). Inserting a user message after a tool result is fine for providers as long as result runs are contiguous. OK.

Wait — actually there's a subtle issue with the anchor extension loop: consider messages `[..., ToolCall(A), ToolResult(A), ToolResult(B)]` where boundary is ToolResult(A) with the marker text. anchor = index of ToolResult(A). Loop: messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage, messages[anchor+1] is ToolResultMessage → anchor++ → now anchor = ToolResult(B); loop checks messages[anchor+1] is ToolResultMessage — if next is an AssistantMessage, stop. Carrier inserted after ToolResult(B). Good — result run intact.

But what if boundary = ToolResult(A), and NEXT is ToolResult(B) which is NOT part of the same run (parallel calls are in the same run anyway). Fine.

2. **The `restoredKeys` window-membership probe cost**: `injectOperativePinCarriers` joins the entire window text every request — `messages.map(_messageText).join('\n')` — on EVERY request (this is in `_buildRequestContext`, per-turn per-request). For a large window (200k tokens ≈ 800KB), that's an 800KB string build per request — plus `windowText.contains(pin.line)` per pin. This is O(window) per request, duplicating work that `serializeConversation` also does. Performance concern — per-request full-window string materialization. The image registry scans messages too, so maybe acceptable pattern-wise, but it's still a real per-request cost: building the joined window text even when the boundary is present. Could short-circuit: only probe per-pin line containment across messages without joining (early exit). IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION.

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

Exploitation requires: consented third-party skill with a pin line containing the literal open tag + that pin riding a summary (the summarizer must reproduce it) + the sanitizer then failing to strip a poisoned ephemeral claim later in that summary. It's a defense-in-depth weakening of the #1131 gate, not direct data loss. The sanitizers' poison-class is "ephemeral claims persist" — moderate severity. I'd keep it IMPORTANT (real hardening gap in a new injection-adjacent surface), not BLOCK — it doesn't break behavior on its own and requires a consented malicious skill (which already has broader powers — its SKILL.md body is read into context anyway!). Actually true: a consented malicious skill's BODY text already enters context un-sanitized; the sanitizer only strips summarizer-echoed ephemeral claims. The marginal gain for an attacker is small. IMPORTANT is right. Good.

So: blocking 2, important 2, suggestions 4-5.

Wait — should finding 2 (app boot) really be blocking? Let me re-read the verdict mapping: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss." A silently-inert feature in one host = broken behavior for that host. OK, blocking. But hmm, one consideration — is there really NO boot path? The relay/`fromAgent` constructors are for tests. So yes — production app sessions never get operativeSkills. Confirmed blocking.

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \

blocks.text:
The coverage run (sh-46) is still going. Meanwhile, let me continue the review:

1. Check `Skill` class — `skill.manifest.operative`, `skill.filePath`, `skill.name` fields exist.
2. Check the `read` tool name and 'path' argument in the actual tool registry.
3. Check `effectiveContextWindow` exists in agent_loop scope.
4. Look at pinned_operative_test.dart (compaction) and open_requests_test.dart (+1).
5. Check the read tool call path — ToolCall.arguments typing.

Also verify the E6 behavior claim: "carriers render only when a compaction/trim boundary exists" — and the interplay with `findCutPoint` keeping ~200 recent tokens: the summary user message sits at the position of the fold; carrier right after it. But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

Also — SkillManifest parsing: `frontmatter['operative']` — what parses the frontmatter into a Map? If the YAML parser resolves `operative:` list items — items are strings. `'$item'` conversion handles non-strings (numbers). OK.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

Wait — actually, let me double check: maybe agent_cli.dart or somewhere sets `operativePinNotice = ...`. My grep covered lib/ bin/ flutter_app/lib/ for operativePinNotice outside operative_pins.dart and found only agent_loop.dart references (the import + use). So no host sets it. Confirmed.

- AC6 notices: `SkillOperativePins.diff` never called in production → supersede/drop notices never rendered anywhere. AC6's "reports the change" unmet. IMPORTANT.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

Let me also check `Skill` class shape and the `read` tool. And `effectiveContextWindow` function.

```dart
final (promptSuffix, enabledSkills) = await _discoverPromptSuffix(...);
...
// in _withEnv, after the agent is built:
_agent.operativeSkills = enabledSkills;

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

blocks.text:
The coverage run (sh-46) is still going. Meanwhile, let me continue the review:

1. Check `Skill` class — `skill.manifest.operative`, `skill.filePath`, `skill.name` fields exist.
2. Check the `read` tool name and 'path' argument in the actual tool registry.
3. Check `effectiveContextWindow` exists in agent_loop scope.
4. Look at pinned_operative_test.dart (compaction) and open_requests_test.dart (+1).
5. Check the read tool call path — ToolCall.arguments typing.

Also verify the E6 behavior claim: "carriers render only when a compaction/trim boundary exists" — and the interplay with `findCutPoint` keeping ~200 recent tokens: the summary user message sits at the position of the fold; carrier right after it. But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

Also — SkillManifest parsing: `frontmatter['operative']` — what parses the frontmatter into a Map? If the YAML parser resolves `operative:` list items — items are strings. `'$item'` conversion handles non-strings (numbers). OK.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

Wait — actually, let me double check: maybe agent_cli.dart or somewhere sets `operativePinNotice = ...`. My grep covered lib/ bin/ flutter_app/lib/ for operativePinNotice outside operative_pins.dart and found only agent_loop.dart references (the import + use). So no host sets it. Confirmed.

- AC6 notices: `SkillOperativePins.diff` never called in production → supersede/drop notices never rendered anywhere. AC6's "reports the change" unmet. IMPORTANT.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

Let me also check `Skill` class shape and the `read` tool. And `effectiveContextWindow` function.

blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. blocks.text:
# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

5. Check the read tool call path — ToolCall.arguments typing.

Also verify the E6 behavior claim: "carriers render only when a compaction/trim boundary exists" — and the interplay with `findCutPoint` keeping ~200 recent tokens: the summary user message sits at the position of the fold; carrier right after it. But consider MULTIPLE folds: boundary search takes the LAST boundary — good.

One more potential issue injectOperativePinCarriers: the anchor-extension loop:
```dart
while (anchor + 1 < messages.length &&
    messages[anchor + 1] is ToolResultMessage &&
    messages[anchor] is ToolResultMessage) {
  anchor++;
}
```
If boundary is a UserMessage followed by ToolResultMessage (can that happen in a payload after image-registry rewrite? A tool result directly after a user message would be malformed; pairing repair happens after injection — "Runs BEFORE tool-pairing repair"). If the window contains an orphan tool-result at the very start (after trim), and the boundary is elsewhere... the carrier would be inserted before the orphan result — pairing repair then handles. Edge, fine.

Bigger question — the timestamp of the carrier: `messages[anchor].timestamp` — same timestamp as the boundary message. Then messages list has two messages with identical timestamps; any downstream ordering by timestamp could reorder. Probably fine (list order preserved).

Also — `injectOperativePinCarriers` returns the SAME list instance when nothing to inject (`return messages`), and agent_loop checks `identical(injected, requestContext.messages)` — fine.

Performance: `windowText` join per request. For every request in a pin-carrying session with a boundary present, we join the ENTIRE window (~ hundreds of KB) just to test `contains(pin.line)` per pin. Also note `_messageText` for UserMessage with content List casts `content as List<ContentBlock>` — UserMessage content type is `String | List<ContentBlock>`? Let me confirm the UserMessage.content type union — if it's `dynamic`, the cast is safe-ish.

Next: `readSkillPathsInWindow` matches `block.name != 'read'` — check the actual read tool registration name and whether skills are READ via the `read` tool with `path` argument. In this harness, read tool: lib/src/tools/read.dart? Let me check quickly.

Also — SkillManifest parsing: `frontmatter['operative']` — what parses the frontmatter into a Map? If the YAML parser resolves `operative:` list items — items are strings. `'$item'` conversion handles non-strings (numbers). OK.

One more: `skill_manifest.dart` — over-cap line rejected with note; note message uses `label('operative')`. Fine.

Security review of the whole thing:
- Pins ride as a UserMessage in the request — the ticket says "pins are rendered as notice text, never as system-role instructions and never as user input". BUT the carrier IS a UserMessage! `UserMessage(content: block, ...)` — the ticket's threat model says pins must be "never ... as user input". The carrier is literally injected as a user-role message. Hmm — the image carriers are presumably also UserMessages (the precedent). The doc in operative_pins.dart says "pins are rendered as notice TEXT inside a harness-generated fixed wrapper, never as system-role instructions and never as user input" — but `injectOperativePinCarriers` creates `UserMessage(content: block)`. That IS user input from the provider's perspective (role: user). The claim contradicts the implementation. In practice it's how image carriers work too, and the wrapper frames it. But strictly, the security claim "never as user input" is false in the implementation — the pinned block arrives in the user role, which is MORE privileged for injection than tool results. The ticket's E8: "notice block framing is generated by the harness (fixed wrapper text, content-keyed inner line), impersonation is text inside inert quotes" — the harness wrapper is fixed; content is quoted. But role-wise it's a user message. Is this a finding? The ticket explicitly promises "pins cannot ... be rendered ... as user input". The implementation violates that promise. However, the alternative (system-prompt injection) is heavier per-request. I'd flag as IMPORTANT security-posture doc/impl mismatch (or accept user-role as the carrier channel and fix the docs/threat model). Given the PR's own security posture statements, this is a fair IMPORTANT finding.

- Prompt-injection amplifier: acknowledged in the ticket; mitigations: consent (F7), 512-char cap, budget, provenance, inert quoting. The hostile corpus test exists. Decent.

- The `restoredKeys` notice and `operativePinNotice` — no host sets it → notices silently dropped (P6 "never silent" unmet at host level; the drop still bounds payload, but the operator audit trail is absent). IMPORTANT (mechanism invariant claims never-silent; hosts don't wire the callback).

- AC6 notices: `SkillOperativePins.diff` never called in production → supersede/drop notices never rendered anywhere. AC6's "reports the change" unmet. IMPORTANT.

- AC5 resume re-inject: `formatOperativePinsForPrompt` never called in production. But the E2E test claims "E2E-PIN-2/AC5: resume over the same JSONL — pin present, zero SKILL.md reads". How does the pin get present on resume if not via formatOperativePinsForPrompt? Via the carrier injection (the resumed window contains the compaction summary boundary → carrier re-injected at request assembly). So AC5's mechanism is satisfied through the carrier, and the ticket's "index-channel notice" variant isn't implemented. The exported dead function is dead code. Let me verify the e2e test asserts request-level presence. Let me read the integration test quickly.

- AC10 mentioned in PR description ("Consent inheritance: ... (AC10)") — no AC10 in ticket (only AC1-AC9). Minor doc sloppiness in PR description.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Flutter app never publishes `operativeSkills` at boot — the feature is silently inert in the app host**

`AgentService.create` computes the enabled skills but **discards them**:

final promptSuffixResult = await _discoverPromptSuffix(

final promptSuffix = promptSuffixResult.$1;   // $2 (enabled skills) dropped

The only three sites that assign `_agent.operativeSkills` are `setSkillsAccess` (early-returns when the consent is unchanged), `setSkillToggle` (fires only on a user toggle), and the wiring twin of the former. On a fresh app session none of them runs, so `_agent.operativeSkills` stays `const []`:

- no pin carrier is ever injected into requests (agent_loop guard `config.operativeSkills.isNotEmpty` is false), and
- `agent_service_compaction.dart:310` forwards an empty list, so every app summarization prompt is byte-identical to the pre-pin pipeline.

Net effect: in the Flutter app the whole gh-1409 mechanism is a silent no-op until the user touches skill settings — AC2/AC3 are unmet for that host, with no error and no notice, while the PR description lists the app wiring as a key decision. The CLI path is correct (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:155` publishes at boot).

Fix: destructure in `create` and thread the list into `_withEnv` (mirroring the CLI):

```dart
final (promptSuffix, enabledSkills) = await _discoverPromptSuffix(...);
...
// in _withEnv, after the agent is built:
_agent.operativeSkills = enabledSkills;
```
